decision: Allow an include to be written as a mapping: a `$ref: file:...` key, with the other keys acting as overrides deep-merged into the included content (mappings merge key by key, anything else replaces)
A new key under content from an included file is written into the including file as an override, and the shared included file is left untouched

When a key is added, a scalar-form include is rewritten in mapping form (`key:  # c` / `$ref: file:...` / new keys), using the file's own indentation, keeping the original quoting and keeping the end-of-line comment on the key line
An existing value changes where it is set: in the override if there is one, otherwise in the file it comes from
Appending a list item, or adding a key inside a list item, still writes to the file that holds the list (no override)
Change the existing test_include_refused so it expects coder.yaml to be left alone, replacing the earlier expectation that a new key is written into it

decision: 'The including file' means one level up: with nested includes, the new key goes into the file that directly includes the source, even if that file is itself included
A section already in mapping form takes new keys next to its existing overrides
A file whose whole content is an include (`file:b.yml`) is converted to `$ref: file:b.yml` plus the new keys at the top level
A scalar-form include inside a flow collection is converted to a flow mapping `{$ref: ..., k: v}`
A scalar-form include that is a block list item becomes `- $ref: file:...` with the overrides aligned below it, using a width of max(2, indent)
If the `file:` string is not on the same line as its key or dash, converting it is refused with exit 3 instead of reflowing the lines
A `$ref` whose value is not a `file:` string is an error (exit 4); so is a mapping-form text include that has sibling keys. A mapping-form include holding only `$ref` is exactly the include
If the included YAML is not a mapping, overrides (a mapping) replace it; with no overrides, the included value is returned unchanged
reason: Follows the merge rule that anything other than two mappings is replaced
